levels.title: What does a valid split look like?
levels.body_md:
We need two parts that add to `w`. Both parts must be positive and even.

What does that tell you about `w`? Try to split a few tiny numbers in your head.
levels.question_back: Can you try to split `1`, `2`, `3`, `4` by hand? Which ones feel possible?

levels.title: Parity and size observations
levels.body_md:
The sum of two even numbers has a special parity. That already rules out many values of `w`.

Also each part is positive, so it cannot be too tiny. It must have some minimum size.

levels.title: Think brute force plus math
levels.body_md:
This is a math and brute force task. The limits for `w` are very small.

It fits because you only need parity reasoning plus a check for very small totals. You could also just try all pairs.

levels.title: Outline of the check
levels.body_md:
In words: think what parity the total of two evens must have. Then think what the smallest possible total of two positive evens is.

Combine those two ideas to test `w`. Trying all possible first parts also works. This takes constant time and memory.
